Tamaulipas officials presented expansion and modernization plans for Nuevo Laredo's World Trade Bridge to a delegation from Mexico's foreign trade business council, COMCE, during a visit to the bridge on October 30, 2026, according to La Noticia de Matamoros.

The visit took place during COMCE's 32nd National Congress. Luis Armando Cantú, Tamaulipas' undersecretary for sustainable development, competitiveness and foreign trade, led the tour, which also included the state government offices at the crossing and the new headquarters building of Mexico's National Customs Agency (ANAM) in Nuevo Laredo.

According to the report, the projects are meant to strengthen the bridge's operating capacity, improve freight flow, and meet the needs of international trade — consolidating Nuevo Laredo's position as one of Mexico's leading border crossings. The delegation was headed by COMCE director general Susana Dique Romero, and Nuevo Laredo customs administrator Lt. Col. Eric Omar Salinas joined the tour.

Cantú said the work fits into Gov. Américo Villarreal Anaya's economic development strategy: strengthening border infrastructure, consolidating Tamaulipas' logistics role, and creating better conditions for economic growth and international trade.

Sources:

  • La Noticia de Matamoros, "Presenta Tamaulipas proyectos de modernización del Puente del Comercio Mundial a delegación de COMCE," October 30, 2026
